clue.text: Does it show church is beset by extremes in storm?

definitions.text: Does it show church is beset by extremes in storm?

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the church and 'is' sit inside the other letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether a church caught up in a storm shows what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: a church caught in a storm of dispute is exactly what splits into factions.
explanation.definitionFit: A split within a church is the classic case of a division between factions, which the clue's storm-struck church shows.

clue.text: Fuse fuel leak from a container, save a penny

parts.note: coal is a fuel

indicators.note: save in its old sense of except, so these letters are left out

parts.note: to escape is to leak out of a vessel
A as written plus P, the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Instructions for joining something while fuel seeps from a can, minus a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' is the old preposition meaning except, not the verb of rescue; the penny is the abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to join together into one mass or whole.

clue.text: Among everything else, Henry's abandoned intrigue

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: Henry has abandoned the phrase, so his letter is dropped from it

parts.note: everything else is the rest
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Among all the rest, Henry has given up on some plot.
explanation.walkthrough: IN THE REST loses its H to give the answer; 'Henry's' reads as 'Henry has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrigue someone is to arouse their curiosity, the same as to hold their attention or concern, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Outcome in tussle against Russian 14

indicators.note: the outcome is placed inside the tussle

parts.note: a melee is a confused scuffle
an outcome is an end
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A result emerges from a scuffle with a Russian scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is SCIENTIST, so the definition is a Russian scientist: Dmitri Mendeleev, who drew up the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendeleev was the Russian chemist behind the periodic table, an example of a Russian scientist.

clue.text: Flatter and knock clean over

parts.note: to butt is to knock with the head

indicators.note: over signals that the word for clean is turned back to front

parts.note: pure means clean

explanation.surface: Praise someone, then knock them flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the word for clean; 'and' joins definition to wordplay, so 'knock clean over' is not one action.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is an idiom for flattering them to win favour.

clue.text: Mathematician errs — last blunder is awful

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who gets numbers wrong makes one last terrible mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is awful' rearranges the letters of ERRS LAST BLUNDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell co-wrote Principia Mathematica, a noted British logician and philosopher of numbers.

clue.text: Maze escapee essays run around Ulster's capital

indicators.note: the essays run around, enclosing the letter

parts.note: theses are long academic essays

indicators.note: a capital is a head or first letter

explanation.surface: Essays circle the head of Ulster, set by someone fleeing a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' gives U, the first letter of Ulster, which 'run around' puts inside THESES.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Theseus killed the Minotaur and found his way out of the labyrinth with Ariadne's thread.

clue.text: Bags I get on this fine estate, say, erected inside castle

indicators.note: the fine and car go inside the castle

parts.note: a rook is the chess piece also called a castle
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: in a down clue erected means written upwards, so the car is reversed

parts.note: an estate car is one kind of car

explanation.surface: Someone claims first dibs on a fine estate built inside a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' reverses the car; 'Bags I' is a British children's claim to first dibs, but here bags are luggage on top of a car. An estate is a British station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack fixed on a car's roof is where luggage bags are carried.

clue.text: Not looking well, with stitch and knot twisted at their join?

indicators.note: where the two words meet their touching letters are twisted round

parts.note: purl is a knitting stitch
to bind is to tie or knot

explanation.surface: A knitter struggles with a stitch and a knot that tangle where they meet.
explanation.walkthrough: PURL and BIND meet at L and B; 'twisted at their join' swaps those two so PURLBIND becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Purblind means partly sighted, so unable to see properly.

clue.text: Zip perhaps provided by accelerator?

definitions.meaning: a zip is one kind of device that closes clothing
jokingly, something that makes things fast, as a lightener makes things light

explanation.surface: A zip might be what a speeding device provides.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading plays on 'fast-en' as 'make faster', which is not its real sense; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: A zip is an example of a fastening device; the joke sense treats one who makes things fast as an accelerator.

clue.text: Brief time in Israeli PM's life?

indicators.note: the brief time goes inside the prime minister's name

parts.note: Golda Meir was Prime Minister of Israel
a mo, short for moment, is a brief time

explanation.surface: A short spell in an Israeli prime minister's life story.
explanation.walkthrough: Golda Meir was Israel's prime minister in the 1970s; 'life' as a biography is why the clue ends in a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A life can mean a written account of someone's history, as a memoir is.

clue.text: I strongly approve of the woman nursing a grassland bird

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the woman's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: her refers to a woman
taken as written
the rhea is a flightless bird of South American grasslands

explanation.surface: A speaker praises a woman caring for a prairie bird.
explanation.walkthrough: HER holds A plus RHEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is called out in Parliament or meetings to show emphatic agreement.

clue.text: The juice is not quite one's favourite part

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A drink described as not quite someone's preferred bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the last letter from the whole phrase; 'juice' is informal for fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is informal for fuel such as motor spirit.

clue.text: Town in Suffolk expanding nine suburbs' borders

indicators.note: borders are the outer edges, so each word gives its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Suffolk town spreads out across the edges of nine suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of four words: SK, EG, NE, SS. Skegness is actually a Lincolnshire seaside resort, so 'in Suffolk' is purely wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Skegness is an English seaside resort on the Lincolnshire coast.

clue.text: Cologne is top in trials involving one researcher

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the one goes inside

parts.note: eau de cologne is a scent
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Cologne leads in product trials checked by a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top in' takes the first letter of trials; 'involving' puts the one inside the cologne word, so that it splits the scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist carries out systematic research, so researcher is a fair broad synonym.

clue.text: First pair of webbed feet crossing line served by a shuttle?

definitions.text: crossing line served by a shuttle?

indicators.note: the first two letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A duck's webbed feet cross a line on a ferry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'First pair of' takes WE from webbed. On a loom the shuttle carries the crosswise threads.
explanation.definitionFit: In weaving the crosswise threads, carried by the shuttle, cross the lengthwise warp.

clue.text: What's on one's plate? Stewed woodlark

indicators.note: stewed food is cooked into a mush, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A diner finds a cooked songbird served up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stewed' rearranges WOODLARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a lot on your plate is an idiom for having many tasks to deal with.

clue.text: Not afraid of Ecstasy in a much smaller amount

indicators.note: in places the drug's letter inside the phrase for a much smaller amount

parts.note: far less is a much smaller amount
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone unafraid of the drug taken in smaller doses.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside FAR LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless means having no fear, which is the same as not being afraid.

clue.text: A runner on snow would

parts.note: to ski is to go on snow

explanation.surface: A runner on snow would do so.
explanation.walkthrough: SKI then D, from the 'd of I'd for I would.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a runner, as on the undercarriage of a helicopter or a sledge.

clue.text: Apparent explanation for Essex's appeal?

parts.note: the name of the county read as letters: E S S around a sex, so the name explains its attraction

explanation.surface: Why is the county of Essex so attractive?
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SEX IN ESS, the answer seems to describe the letters of Essex. Essex is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexiness is physical attractiveness, the jokey reason given for the county's appeal.

clue.text: Crowd, in comparison with absent leader, is rooted

indicators.note: the crowd is put in, placed inside the shortened comparison word
the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a simile is a figure of speech comparing things
a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A leaderless crowd stands still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with absent leader' drops the first letter of the comparison word, then 'in' sets the crowd inside what remains; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooted to the spot means unable to move, which is what immobile says.

clue.text: A set of teeth used in Esperanto verb iterations

indicators.note: the answer is used inside these words, running across them

explanation.surface: A grammar point about repeating verbs in Esperanto.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of Esperanto through verb into iterations.
explanation.definitionFit: An overbite is a set of upper teeth jutting over the lower ones.

clue.text: Reduced upfront price for work

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: upfront means open and frank
a rate is a price

explanation.surface: A cut upfront cost for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: OPEN loses its last letter for OPE, then RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works.

clue.text: Core sailors in bottom of ship

indicators.note: the sailors are in the ship's bottom, placed inside that word

parts.note: the keel runs along the bottom of a ship
RN is the Royal Navy, hence sailors

explanation.surface: A crew lives at the heart of a ship's lowest part.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy stands for sailors in general, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the central or essential part of something, its core.

clue.text: Manager with perm almost converted to new shade

indicators.note: one part of the word is changed into another

parts.note: a supervisor manages staff

indicators.note: almost means all but the last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boss with a permed hairdo changes to a new style of hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts PERM to PER; in SUPERVISOR, PER becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun visor gives shade from glare, so it is a kind of shade.

clue.text: Perhaps unrequited love experienced for the first time, yes?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
something new is met for the first time
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: Is unrequited love something felt for the first time?
explanation.walkthrough: O + NEW + AY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrequited love goes in one direction only, so it is an example of a love running only one way.

clue.text: Death reduced by a third in large-scale outbreak

indicators.note: the shortened death goes inside

parts.note: an epic is grand and large-scale

indicators.note: six letters lose two, a third

parts.note: demise means death

explanation.surface: Deaths cut by a third in a widespread outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by a third' cuts two letters from the six-letter word for death; 'in' puts the remainder inside the word for large-scale.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a widespread outbreak of disease.

clue.text: Ruffle fiendish she-devil

indicators.note: fiendish suggests something wild and twisted, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A wicked female demon messes things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiendish' rearranges SHE-DEVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to make hair or clothes untidy, to ruffle them.

clue.text: Turk's worried about English origin for Merchant Ivory?

indicators.note: the letters go round the abbreviation for English
worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: the letters of Turks

explanation.surface: A Turkish man fretting about an English film company's roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges TURKS to TUSKR, round E. Merchant Ivory were film makers; here ivory sold by a merchant comes from an elephant's tusks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusker is an elephant with large tusks, the source of ivory sold by merchants.
